title: Data pipeline (batch ETL, transforms, curation)
confidence_notes: Code whose job is to read data from one place and write transformed data to another, in batch. Signals: a DAG or workflow file, raw and processed data directories, golden or expected outputs, a schema or validation dependency, SQL models. Distinguish from ml-training (no optimizer loop) and science-sim (output is a dataset, not a scalar quality). If the transforms live in a package with tests, stack python-package. A golden output (a checked-in expected result for a fixed input) is the instrument; if none exists, the first campaign is an instrument campaign that records one from the current code and freezes it.

default_cards.title: End-to-end wall-clock of `{{run_command}}` on the fixture input
gaming_risks: work skipped when the output already exists (the command removes the output dir first; a diff that writes to a different cache location is the workaround)
rows dropped, columns dropped, or a transform stubbed (golden_diff_lines and row_count must hold)
the fixture input detected by name or size and handled by a fast path (the holdout input exists for this)
an intermediate cached on disk between screen and confirm outside the output dir
thread count raised through the environment outside a declared config hypothesis

default_cards.title: Output rows per second of wall-clock

measure.command:
rm -rf {{output_dir}}; python3 -c 'import subprocess,time,sys,os,glob
t=time.perf_counter()
r=subprocess.run("{{run_command}}", shell=True, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
dt=time.perf_counter()-t
if r.returncode: sys.exit(r.returncode)
n=sum(sum(1 for _ in open(f, "rb")) - 1 for f in glob.glob("{{output_dir}}/*.csv"))
print("METRIC rows_per_s=%.1f" % (n/dt))'

gaming_risks: duplicate rows emitted to inflate the numerator (row_count is an equal guardrail)
rows counted from a file the pipeline no longer fully writes (parquet outputs are not counted here; adjust the glob to the real format)

default_cards.title: Lines differing between sorted output and the golden output

measure.command: rm -rf {{output_dir}}; {{run_command}} >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; [ -f {{golden_path}} ] || exit 3; LC_ALL=C sort {{output_path}} > .sb-out.sorted; LC_ALL=C sort {{golden_path}} > .sb-gold.sorted; n=$(diff .sb-out.sorted .sb-gold.sorted | grep -c '^[<>]'); echo "METRIC golden_diff_lines=$n"

gaming_risks: floating-point formatting changed so lines differ for a reason the pipeline's users would accept: the metrologist should decide the comparison tolerance at INSTRUMENT, not the experimenter later
output written to a different path while {{output_path}} is stale or copied from golden (a diff that copies from a golden path is gamed)
column order or sort order changed: the sort makes row order irrelevant, column order still matters

default_cards.title: Output columns missing from or extra to the declared schema

measure.command: [ -f {{output_path}} ] || { rm -rf {{output_dir}}; {{run_command}} >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; }; python3 -c 'import csv,json; h=next(csv.reader(open("{{output_path}}", newline=""))); exp=json.load(open("{{schema_path}}"))["columns"]; print("METRIC schema_violations=%d" % len(set(exp) ^ set(h)))'

gaming_risks: column names kept while their contents changed type or meaning (a pandera or great_expectations suite is the stronger instrument; use it when present)
the schema file read from a non-frozen copy

default_cards.title: Output row count on the fixture input

measure.command: [ -f {{output_path}} ] || { rm -rf {{output_dir}}; {{run_command}} >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 1; }; n=$(( $(wc -l < {{output_path}} | tr -d ' ') - 1 )); echo "METRIC row_count=$n"

gaming_risks: rows dropped and padded with duplicates to keep the count (golden_diff_lines catches it on the fixture, the holdout input catches a fixture-specific pad)
a header-less output that shifts the count by one

default_cards.title: Peak resident memory of the pipeline process tree

measure.command: rm -rf {{output_dir}}; python3 -c 'import resource,subprocess,sys; r=subprocess.run("{{run_command}}", shell=True, stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL); m=resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_CHILDREN).ru_maxrss; print("METRIC peak_mem_mb=%.1f" % (m/(1024*1024) if sys.platform=="darwin" else m/1024)); sys.exit(r.returncode)'

gaming_risks: ru_maxrss reports the largest single child, not the sum, for a multi-process pipeline (spark, dask): note it on the card and prefer the framework's own peak metric
memory traded for runtime by spilling to disk without declaring it

noise_sources: I/O contention and page cache state (the first run after checkout reads from disk, later runs from cache; screen repeats should discard the first)
thread pools sized from the machine (pin OMP_NUM_THREADS, POLARS_MAX_THREADS, RAYON_NUM_THREADS)
a cloud or database source with variable latency (the fixture input must be local for the latency cards to mean anything)
temporary files from a previous run left in the output dir (every timed command removes it first)
notes: The pipeline must read its input from SB_INPUT and write to SB_OUTPUT (or take equivalent flags the metrologist wires into {{run_command}}); the fixture input is a small, checked-in slice under data/fixtures/, the holdout input is a second slice the experimenter never sees, copied in by the harness under .strictlybetter/holdout/pipeline_input/. {{output_path}} is the main CSV the golden is checked against; for parquet or a database target replace the sort-and-diff with the framework's own comparison and keep the same METRIC line. dependency is warmer here than in most packs because moving a transform from pandas to polars or duckdb is the most common honest runtime win. Cost per run for a cloud pipeline is in the docs/07 table; it is not shipped as a card because it depends on the provider's billing API; if the project has a cost printout, wrap it as a metric-line card named cost_per_run_usd. golden_diff_lines with tolerance 0 is strict; if the pipeline is legitimately nondeterministic in float formatting, the metrologist rounds inside the comparison at INSTRUMENT and freezes that comparison script.
